item.content:encoded:
多频道新闻雷达 — 经济新闻

2026-07-30 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 114 · 生成时间: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

板块速览

今日全球市场在美伊冲突升级与AI板块剧烈分化中震荡。美国突袭伊朗后油价飙升，欧洲股市承压；FOMC维持利率不变但长端收益率跳升，市场质疑美联储抗通胀决心。科技股方面，微软财报强劲并扩大资本开支，但AI板块整体下行，中际旭创港股首日破发，科创50跌超6%。中国央行加码逆回购维稳资金面，金饰价格突破1239元/克。后续观察美伊冲突对能源通胀的传导、FOMC会后言论对加息预期的影响，以及AI投资从硬件向应用端轮动的可能。

  • U.S. strikes Iran after surprise missile attack, dashing hopes of de-escalation — 美国与伊朗全面开战，霍尔木兹海峡危机深化，全球油价面临进一步上行压力。
  • Microsoft jumps 8% as it boosts capital spending plans, citing demand — 微软财报超预期并上调资本开支，股价大涨8%，带动科技巨头AI军备竞赛预期。
  • Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement — 美联储维持利率不变，但长期国债收益率走高，市场对主席Warsh的信用产生质疑。
  • China threatens retaliation against U.S. humanoid robot ban — 中国商务部威胁反制美国对人形机器人的禁令，中美科技脱钩再添新战线。
  • Zhongji Innolight shares fall on Hong Kong debut amid global AI sell-off — 中际旭创港股上市首日跌近3%，反映AI光模块短期估值压力。
  • ECB wage tracker at 2.7% in Q1 2027 — 欧央行工资跟踪器显示谈判工资增速稳定在2.7%，为后续政策提供参考。
  • 多家金店金饰价格集体上涨，最高报1239元/克 — 国内金价受避险情绪推动创历史新高，投资者关注黄金配置机会。

后续观察：美伊冲突是否引发更大范围供应中断，以及FOMC后续言论对市场的引导。AI板块内部估值分化加剧，建议关注业绩确定性强的算力基础设施与下游应用端。

美股 · 60 条

美伊冲突骤然升级，美国对伊朗发动空袭，油价飙升，避险情绪推高国债价格。与此同时，微软财报超预期并宣布加大资本开支，股价大涨8%，提振科技板块信心。FOMC维持利率不变，但长期收益率走高，市场开始质疑主席Warsh的抗通胀信誉。AI军备竞赛持续，Zuckerberg 在Meta财报中透露AI算力分配困境，而**SpaceX** 被众议院能源委员会要求公开AI数据中心记录。此外，美国正推动亚洲采用其AI，但**中国凭借廉价模型占据优势**。短期看，地缘风险与科技财报博弈将主导美股波动。

欧洲经济 · 13 条

欧洲股市受美伊冲突拖累收盘走低，油价攀升加剧通胀忧虑。欧央行最新工资跟踪器显示Q1 2027谈判工资增速2.7%，暗示薪资压力稳定，但**Morningstar分析** 质疑高能源价格是否迫使欧央行加息。宝马宣布**裁员8000人，主因中国竞争对手压力，显示欧洲汽车业困境。正面消息是爱尔兰经济恢复增长**，提振欧元区信心。欧洲经济面临能源成本、外部竞争与货币政策的三重考验。

中国经济 · 31 条

今日A股在“韩流”冲击下企稳，科创50指数一度跌超6%，但宽基ETF放量护盘。中际旭创港股首日破发，反映全球AI情绪转冷，但其背后是**长鑫存储IPO** 带来的替代预期——中国DRAM产能崛起正在重塑全球半导体格局。与此同时，MLCC企业 利润大涨，显示AI基础设施仍为中国电子产业链提供支撑。央行开展**2705亿+6000亿逆回购** 维护流动性。香港方面，CMU链接瑞士西班牙 扩大国际互联。短期看，中国股市受外部波动影响，但政策托底与国产替代逻辑仍提供韧性。

item.content:encoded:
News Radar — 经济新闻

2026-07-30 · Window: 24h · Items: 114 · Generated: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

Editor's Brief

Global markets are navigating a volatile landscape shaped by the sudden escalation of US-Iran military conflict, which has driven oil prices higher and dampened risk appetite, even as strong tech earnings from Microsoft and Samsung provide a counterbalance. The Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady has drawn criticism over its commitment to fighting inflation, while China accelerates its semiconductor self-sufficiency push with major IPOs and component demand. The following developments defined the past 24 hours:

  • US-Iran conflict reignites: US forces launched strikes against Iran following a surprise missile attack, dashing hopes of de-escalation and pushing oil prices higher (US strikes Iran). The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with Iran rejecting an Omani proposal (Oil climbs).

  • Microsoft surges 8% on earnings: The tech giant boosted capital spending plans, citing strong AI demand, and signaled positive free cash flow for the new fiscal year (Microsoft jumps). This helped offset broader market jitters.

  • Fed credibility under fire: The FOMC left rates unchanged, but long-term Treasury yields jumped as investors question whether Chairman Warsh will act forcefully enough on inflation (Fed credibility).

  • China threatens retaliation over US robot ban: Beijing said the US humanoid robot ban 'severely damages' relations and hinted at countermeasures (China threatens). The US wants Asia to use its AI, but China dominates cheaper models (US vs China AI).

  • BMW to cut up to 8,000 jobs in Germany under pressure from Chinese rivals, highlighting the competitive threat to European automakers (BMW cuts).

  • China's AI supply chain goes public: Zhongji Innolight, a key optical transceiver maker, fell on its Hong Kong debut amid a global AI sell-off (Innolight falls). Meanwhile, CXMT's $9.8 billion Shanghai IPO signaled China's growing DRAM capabilities (CXMT shock).

  • ECB wage tracker stable at 2.7%, but higher energy prices from the Iran conflict could force the ECB to reconsider its rate path (ECB wage, Inflation outlook).

Watch next: All eyes are on the trajectory of US-Iran tensions and their impact on oil prices and global risk sentiment. The Fed's next moves will be scrutinized as inflation expectations adjust. In tech, the AI earnings season continues to bifurcate winners (Microsoft, Samsung) from suppliers exposed to cyclical demand (Innolight). Europe's economic resilience will be tested by both energy costs and Chinese competition, while China's AI self-sufficiency drive accelerates with new listings and component surpluses.

美股 · 60 items

US equities ended a turbulent session mixed, as the outbreak of US-Iran military strikes sent crude soaring and weighed on cyclical sectors, but a powerful rally in Microsoft shares on stellar earnings provided a stark counterbalance. The Federal Reserve held rates steady but faced renewed credibility questions after long-term Treasury yields jumped, and the Senate postponed a key AG nomination vote amid tensions over IRS audits.

  • US strikes Iran: Military action against Iran after a missile attack reignited open conflict, sending oil prices higher and raising risks for global supply chains and inflation (US strikes Iran).
  • Microsoft jumps 8%: The company boosted capital spending plans citing AI demand, and changed accounting for data centers to signal positive free cash flow (Microsoft earnings).
  • Fed leaves rates unchanged: The FOMC statement disappointed markets that had hoped for a more hawkish tone, and long-term yields rose as Chairman Warsh's inflation-fighting credibility came into question (Fed credibility).
  • Samsung beats estimates: Q2 operating profit topped expectations on soaring AI chip demand, extending its record run (Samsung earnings).
  • China threatens retaliation: Beijing condemned the US humanoid robot ban as 'severely damaging' ties and vowed countermeasures, adding a new layer of tech trade tension (China robot ban).

Signal: The market is pricing a sharp divergence between AI winners and geopolitical losers; next week's Fed commentary and Iran developments will determine whether the tech rally can sustain itself amid macro headwinds.

欧洲经济 · 13 items

European stocks closed mostly lower as escalating US-Iran tensions pushed oil prices higher and raised stagflation fears. The ECB's latest wage tracker showed stable negotiated wage growth at 2.7%, but analysts now question whether the central bank can avoid raising rates if energy prices keep climbing. BMW's announcement of up to 8,000 job cuts underlines the existential threat Chinese EV and tech rivals pose to legacy European industry.

  • Stocks lower on geopolitical risk: European indices fell as the US-Iran conflict intensified, with oil prices climbing again after Iran rejected an Omani proposal on the Strait of Hormuz (European markets wrap).
  • ECB wage tracker at 2.7%: Q1 2027 data shows stable negotiated wage pressures, providing some comfort but not enough to offset energy-driven inflation risks (ECB wage).
  • BMW to cut 'as many as 8,000 jobs': The German automaker's voluntary redundancy program targets admin and development roles, directly attributing pressure to Chinese rivals (BMW cuts).
  • Irish economy returns to growth: GDP rebounded, boosting Eurozone growth hopes and offering a counterpoint to broader weakness (Irish growth).
  • Eurozone inflation outlook: Rising energy prices from the Iran conflict could force the ECB to raise rates, complicating the growth outlook (Inflation outlook).

Signal: Europe’s industrial heartland is squeezed between rising energy costs from the Middle East and fierce Chinese competition, making the ECB’s monetary policy path increasingly uncertain.

中国经济 · 31 items

Chinese markets showed resilience amid the global AI sell-off, with the broader market rising as ETF inflows provided support, but AI-related names like Zhongji Innolight struggled on debut. The semiconductor self-sufficiency narrative gained traction with CXMT’s $9.8 billion IPO and surging profits for MLCC makers. Hong Kong faced contagion from South Korea’s tech rout, prompting regulator intervention.

  • Zhongji Innolight debuts lower: The optical transceiver maker fell up to 3% on Hong Kong's biggest share sale of 2026, caught in the global AI demand downturn (Innolight falls).
  • CXMT shock challenges incumbents: ChangXin Memory Technologies’ massive Shanghai IPO underscores China’s push into DRAM, threatening Nvidia, Micron, and SK Hynix (CXMT shock).
  • MLCC makers profit surge: Chinese manufacturers of multilayer ceramic capacitors see explosive first-half earnings driven by AI infrastructure demand (MLCC profits).
  • Hong Kong hit by Korea tech rout: Sharp swings in Samsung and SK Hynix reverberated in Hong Kong, leading to regulatory scrutiny of leveraged products and fund embezzlement cases (HK-Korea contagion).
  • HK expands CMU global reach: The HKMA linked its settlement platform with Switzerland’s SIX, giving access to Swiss and Spanish securities (CMU expansion).

Signal: China’s AI hardware ecosystem is deepening, but near-term sentiment remains hostage to global tech volatility; state-backed ETF inflows and policy support are cushioning the downside.

item.content:encoded:
多频道新闻雷达 — 社会新闻

2026-07-30 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 79 · 生成时间: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

板块速览

过去24小时，全球社会新闻呈现三重焦点：中东冲突骤然升级——美国对伊朗发动“重型”打击，沙特被卷入战火，加沙与黎巴嫩局势同步恶化；日本熊本县发生强烈地震，导致AEON购物中心坍塌，救援仍在进行；欧洲多地山火肆虐，希腊三名消防员殉职，法国持续40℃高温。此外，文化科技领域也有重要动态：萨尔曼·拉什迪袭击者被定罪，数学家王虹与邓煜获菲尔兹奖引发中文社区热议。以下为各区域详细追踪。

  • 中东战火扩大：美伊互袭，沙特陷入两难。美国在伊朗试图攻击美军后发动“重型”打击（BBC），沙特虽试图置身事外却被迫卷入（BBC），美沙联手打击伊拉克境内伊朗支持的民兵（NPR）。同时，以色列空袭加沙城沙提难民营（半岛），黎巴嫩南部村庄因以军“黄线”分裂（半岛）。冲突已冲击全球能源市场，韩国KOSPI指数6%下跌即为明证（MyChamplainValley）。

  • 日本熊本7.0级地震：AEON Mall坍塌，搜救“争分夺秒”。地震发生在29日，导致熊本AEON购物中心严重损毁，首相高市早苗称“与时间赛跑”救援（半岛）。该商场10年前曾因地震重建，刚重新开放（Japan Times）。韩国外交部通报无韩国公民伤亡（koreatimes）。

  • 欧洲山火：希腊三名消防员牺牲，法国居民拒绝撤离。希腊克里特岛遭强风助长野火，三名消防员殉职（BBC）。法国吉伦特地区40℃高温下，部分居民拒绝撤离（BBC）。

  • 萨尔曼·拉什迪袭击者被判恐怖主义罪。28岁的哈迪·马塔尔被认定试图协助真主党，袭击作者（BBC）。

  • 演员杰瑞德·莱托被10名女性指控性侵。其中包括未成年指控，警方已展开调查（BBC）。

  • 韩国女性网络侦探对抗AI深度伪造色情。一群女性志愿者利用技术追踪合成淫秽影像，反映数字性犯罪治理难题（Japan Today）。

  • 中国—东盟教育交流周开幕，聚焦数智教育与AI。第19届交流周在贵州举行，已累计2.09万东盟学子留学贵州（Sohu），另有多条AI赋能教育的实践报道（中国教育新闻网）。

后续观察：中东局势的升级可能进一步推高油价，并引发更广泛的代理战争，沙特能否保持中立将是关键变量。日本熊本地震的救援进展和建筑抗震标准再次受到审视。欧洲山火在极端高温下恐将持续数周，气候变化的直接冲击已不容忽视。文化领域，拉什迪案和莱托案分别折射出言论自由与演艺圈权力结构性弊病。

欧美 · 35 条

中东战火急遽升温，美国与伊朗直接交火，沙特被迫选边；欧洲则面临山火与司法裁决并行。

  • 美伊冲突：打击与反打击循环。美国对伊朗发动“重型”打击，回应伊朗周二对美军的导弹攻击（BBC）。沙特阿拉伯陷入两难——既需威慑也需降温（BBC）。美沙联合空袭伊拉克境内伊朗民兵（NPR）。加沙及黎巴嫩南部同步遭以军打击（半岛），五个月冲突难见尾声，全球经济面临不确定性。
  • 希腊山火致三名消防员殉职，强风令克里特岛多个村庄撤离，南欧多国仍在应对野火（BBC）。
  • 萨尔曼·拉什迪案：被告哈迪·马塔尔被判恐怖主义罪名成立，袭击意在帮助真主党（BBC）。
  • 演员杰瑞德·莱托面临10名女性指控，包括未成年人，律师否认（BBC）。

中东战事与欧洲极端天气是当前欧美社会两大主线，战争的外溢效应（石油、市场、难民）将逐步显现。

日本熊本地震成为核心冲击，韩国市场则受中东冲突波及而剧烈震荡。

  • 韩国股市重挫：KOSPI指数暴跌6%，主因中东战火推升油价（MyChamplainValley）。三星Q2营业利润创纪录达89.5万亿韩元，但市场担忧后续出口受冲突与汇率影响（Korea Herald）。
  • 韩国女性网络侦探自发对抗AI深度伪造色情，展现民间科技维权力量（Japan Today）。

日韩正同时承受自然灾害与地缘经济冲击，日本救援进展与韩国市场情绪将是后续焦点。

2026-07-30 · Window: 24h · Items: 79 · Generated: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

Editor's Brief

The last 24 hours have been dominated by escalating military confrontation between the US and Iran, drawing Saudi Arabia into a widening conflict, while Japan reels from a massive earthquake that has trapped dozens in a collapsed mall and fuelled wildfires across southern Europe. Meanwhile, domestic Chinese news focuses on education reforms and AI integration, and the Zhihu community buzzes with mathematician celebrity scandals and a major hospital corruption case.

多频道新闻雷达 — 军事新闻

2026-07-30 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 62 · 生成时间: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

板块速览

军事新闻板块简报 (2026-07-30)

导语： 过去24小时全球军事态势急剧升温，美伊冲突从空袭扩大到伊拉克战场，中国通过向伊朗提供防空导弹及在南海部署航母编队展现战略介入能力。与此同时，美国海军签署创纪录的潜艇合同，RIMPAC演习推进无人系统实验，台海与印太方向博弈持续深化。

  • 美伊冲突全面升级： 美国以伊朗导弹袭击驻约旦美军未遂为由，联合沙特对伊拉克境内伊朗代理人发动空袭 (NY Post)，特朗普威胁进一步报复 (NBC News)。中国在此背景下被曝向伊朗运送防空导弹 (AOL)，使冲突具有更广泛的地缘博弈色彩。
  • 中国高超音速武器部署加速： 解放军首次在052D型驱逐舰上试射YJ-20高超音速反舰导弹 (TWZ)，加上此前055型搭载的双锥体弹道导弹，中国海军远程打击能力正实现“下沉式”扩散。
  • 南海多国对峙： 美航母坐镇，日本陆上自卫队首次派遣至南海，中国出动航母及26艘舰船“围观” (搜狐)，台海与南海风险交织。
  • 美国海军潜艇合同创纪录： 通用动力和HII获766亿美元合同建造9艘弗吉尼亚级和5艘哥伦比亚级潜艇 (USNI)，反映核威慑与水下力量优先战略。
  • 美台海岸警卫队首次公开联合演练： 美海岸警卫队“米吉特”号与台湾海巡署“台北”舰共同行动 (USNI)，虽未明示地点时间，但标志美台安全合作实质性升级。
  • 欧洲安全焦虑加剧： 北约将领警告俄罗斯可能在2029年前进攻欧洲，而北约要到2035年才能就绪 (Kyiv Post)，推动多国增加国防开支。

后续观察： 美伊对抗已从“报复-反报复”进入多线战场阶段（伊拉克、红海、波斯湾），中国在其中的角色（武器供应、外交表态）将直接影响冲突外溢风险。南海方向，美日欧联合巡航与解放军“围观”形成新常态，需警惕意外交火。美军潜艇合同与高超音速武器扩散则提示大国技术竞赛正加速。

国际安全 · 33 条

概览： 美伊冲突成为绝对焦点，24小时内发生导弹袭击、空袭报复和沙特加入等多重变量。中国向伊朗运送防空导弹的报道为局势增添第三国因素。

  • 美国对伊朗目标实施空袭，此前伊朗导弹袭击驻约旦美军被拦截 (NY Post)，特朗普威胁“报复” (NBC News)。
  • 中国被指在特朗普与习近平“友谊”背景下仍向伊朗提供防空导弹 (AOL)，显示中伊防务合作的战略性。
  • 沙特阿拉伯首次加入美军对伊拉克境内伊朗代理人的空袭 (BBC)，海湾安全格局发生重大重组。
  • 北约与乌克兰启动新反无人机基金 (Breaking Defense)，同时美国考虑授权乌克兰生产“爱国者”系统 (Breaking Defense)，俄乌战场防空压力持续。

判断： 美伊冲突已从代理人战争走向直接军事交锋，且沙特倒向美国阵营将进一步削弱伊朗在阿拉伯世界的立足点。中国向伊朗出口武器可能引发美国新一轮制裁，中美关系面临新考验。

  • 沙特酝酿组建红海联军以反制伊朗支持的组织 (Al-Monitor)，可能与空袭伊拉克同步。

  • 航运业呼吁保护平民海员 (gCaptain)，全球贸易安全成本上升。

判断： 冲突已从也门内战演变为区域海空大战，伊拉克的重返战场表明伊朗与美国的对抗将更持久。胡塞武装的曼德海峡收费威胁若实施，将直接冲击全球能源和贸易流量。

News Radar — 军事新闻

2026-07-30 · Window: 24h · Items: 62 · Generated: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

Editor's Brief

The past 24 hours have witnessed a dramatic escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict, with American forces launching airstrikes on Iranian targets in Iraq and Saudi Arabia joining the operation, while China openly defies Washington by sending anti-air missiles to Tehran. These developments, combined with fresh hypersonic missile tests from the PLA Navy and heightened South China Sea standoffs, signal a broadening theater of competition. Below are the key headlines and their deeper implications for readers tracking global military dynamics.

  • U.S.-Iran conflict erupts into direct strikes – The U.S. military launched airstrikes on Iranian-linked targets in Iraq after foiling a missile attack on American forces. Saudi Arabia participated in the strikes, marking a significant shift in Riyadh’s posture (U.S. launches strikes on Iranian targets). This overt intervention risks drawing Iraq back into a regional war (Iraq once again becomes a battlefield).

  • China sends anti-air missiles to Iran despite Trump-Xi ties – Beijing is reportedly shipping anti-air missiles to Tehran, a direct challenge to U.S. efforts to isolate Iran (China sending anti-air missiles to Iran). This move undermines U.S. coercive diplomacy and signals Chinese alignment with the anti-U.S. axis.

  • PLA tests hypersonic YJ-20 from smaller destroyer – New footage confirms China has integrated the YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship missile onto Type 052D destroyers, not just the larger Type 055. This sharply expands the range of platforms able to strike high-value naval assets (China Fires YJ-20 Hypersonic Anti-Ship Missile).

  • South China Sea standoff: 26 Chinese ships monitor U.S./Japan/EU drills – A U.S. carrier-led flotilla from Japan and Europe entered disputed waters, prompting a heavy PLA response with 26 vessels. This is the largest shadowing operation since 2016 and raises the risk of accidental clash (26艘中国舰船“强势围观”).

  • U.S. Navy awards $76.6B for 14 submarines – After a three-year delay, General Dynamics and HII won contracts for nine Virginia-class and five Columbia-class subs, a critical boost to the nuclear shipbuilding industrial base (Navy Awards $76.6B for 9 Virginia, 5 Columbia Subs).

  • NATO warns Russia may attack Europe by 2029 – Alliance generals assess that Russia could be ready for conventional war against NATO within three years, while NATO force improvements lag until 2035, creating a dangerous readiness gap (Alliance Generals: Russia May Attack Europe by 2029).

  • Ukraine and NATO launch drone countermeasure fund – The Brave1 initiative is funding five priority areas including active protection and electromagnetic attack, reflecting the evolution of the drone war in Ukraine (Ukraine, NATO launch new funding program).

  • Houthis consider tolling Bab al-Mandeb Strait – The Iran-backed group is reportedly mulling charging passage fees through the chokepoint, a move that would escalate maritime economic warfare (Trump Vows Revenge).

Watch next: The U.S.-Iran crisis is entering a new direct kinetic phase, which could trigger a wider confrontation involving Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and proxy forces. Simultaneously, China’s hypersonic missile expansion and South China Sea assertiveness will test U.S.-China crisis management. The NATO readiness warning adds urgency to European defense investment. Readers should monitor the next 48 hours for possible Iranian retaliation or further U.S. strikes.

国际安全 · 33 items

A dramatic escalation: U.S. forces struck Iranian-linked targets in Iraq after thwarting a missile attack on American troops. Saudi Arabia joined the airstrikes, signaling a coalition approach, while China began anti-air missile deliveries to Iran, complicating the strategic picture. Two long-term threat assessments—NATO's warning on Russia and a new Singapore interest in GCAP—round out the desk.

  • U.S. strikes Iran after foiled attack – The U.S. military launched airstrikes on Iranian proxies in Iraq and Syria in response to a failed missile barrage on American forces. This marks the first direct U.S. offensive against Iranian assets under Trump's second term (US military launches airstrikes on Iran).

  • China sends anti-air missiles to Iran – Despite Trump’s claim of friendship with Xi Jinping, Chinese anti-air missiles are headed to Iran, directly aiding a state under U.S. military pressure (China sending anti-air missiles to Iran).

  • NATO warns of Russian attack by 2029 – In a stark assessment, alliance generals state Russia could be ready for conflict with NATO in three years, but NATO won’t meet readiness goals until 2035 (Alliance Generals: Russia May Attack Europe by 2029).

  • Singapore eyes GCAP 6th-gen fighter – Already an F-35 buyer, Singapore is reportedly interested in the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), indicating a shift toward next-generation air power in the Indo-Pacific (Singapore Reportedly Looking Toward 6th Gen Fighter).

Signal: The convergence of U.S.-Iran kinetic strikes, Chinese arms supply to Tehran, and NATO’s urgent war warning suggests a multipolar flashpoint landscape; readers should watch for any second-strike attacks from Iran’s proxies in the next 24 hours.

Iran is testing a more confrontational strategy after striking U.S. forces in Jordan, drawing U.S.-Saudi retaliatory strikes in Iraq. A drone hit on a gas tanker at Egypt's Mediterranean port and Houthi threats to toll the Bab al-Mandeb Strait underscore the widening maritime and energy security risks. The shipping industry is demanding protection for civilian seafarers.

  • Iran tests confrontational strategy – Tehran’s direct missile attack on U.S. troops in Jordan represents a strategic shift from proxy warfare to state-on-state pressure (Tehran tests a more confrontational strategy).

  • Saudi Arabia joins U.S. in Iraq strikes – For the first time, Riyadh participated in airstrikes inside Iraq against Iran-backed militias, a major policy shift that could reshape the regional balance (Saudi Arabia joins US in strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq).

  • Drone hits gas storage tanker at Egyptian port – An explosive-laden drone struck a natural gas tanker at Damietta, Egypt, highlighting the vulnerability of critical energy infrastructure to asymmetric attacks (Drone hits gas storage tanker at Egypt's Mediterranean port).

  • Shipping industry calls for protection of civilian seafarers – As maritime threats surge, industry groups are urging governments to secure sea lines and provide safe passage for crews (Shipping Industry Urges Protection for Civilian Seafarers).

Signal: The spread of conflict from Iraq and Jordan to the Mediterranean and Red Sea pressures global energy routes; a sustained campaign against maritime infrastructure could trigger insurance spikes and supply chain disruptions.

海军与印太 · 7 items

The U.S. Navy finalized a record $76.6 billion submarine contract after long delays, while RIMPAC 2026 pushed unmanned systems interoperability with over 35 experiments. Revelations of U.S.-Taiwan coast guard exercises and AUKUS dry dock design selections show the alliance network deepening in the Indo-Pacific.

  • U.S. Navy awards $76.6B for Virginia- and Columbia-class subs – General Dynamics and HII split contracts for nine Block VI Virginia-class attack subs and five Columbia-class ballistic missile subs, ending a three-year funding gap critical to the nuclear modernization timeline (Navy Awards $76.6B for 9 Virginia, 5 Columbia Subs).

  • RIMPAC runs 35+ unmanned system experiments – During the biennial exercise, U.S. and partner forces tested drones, AI, and autonomous systems to enhance maritime domain awareness and coalition interoperability (More than 35 Experiments Test Unmanned Systems During RIMPAC).

  • U.S. reveals coast guard cooperation with Taiwan – For the first time, the U.S. publicly acknowledged joint exercises between the U.S. Coast Guard and Taiwan’s Coast Guard Administration, a significant step in deepening de facto security ties (U.S. Reveals Coast Guard Cooperation with Taiwan).

  • Australia selects Leidos Gibbs & Cox for AUKUS dry dock – The floating dry dock design contract supports the future AUKUS nuclear-powered submarine maintenance infrastructure, a key enabler of the trilateral pact (Australia Selects Leidos Gibbs & Cox for AUKUS Dry Dock Design).

Signal: The submarine contract renewal and AUKUS infrastructure moves signal sustained U.S. commitment to undersea dominance, but any delays could be offset by Chinese hypersonic anti-ship missile proliferation seen in the China desk.

China is simultaneously showcasing hypersonic strike capability by test-firing the YJ-20 from a Type 052D destroyer, while facing a multi-naval force in the South China Sea with 26 ships. Official commentary highlights military AI development and a Pentagon official's assessment that U.S.-China military relations are the most stable in years—a contradictory signal amid the tensions.

  • YJ-20 hypersonic missile tested from Type 052D destroyer – The People's Liberation Army Navy demonstrated the integration of the YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship missile onto a smaller destroyer, vastly expanding the number of hulls capable of delivering this weapon (China Fires YJ-20 Hypersonic Anti-Ship Missile From Smaller Destroyer and Footage Confirms First Integration of Hypersonic Ballistic Missiles).

  • 26 Chinese ships shadow U.S.-led naval force in South China Sea – Amid the outbreak of U.S.-Iran strikes, a carrier strike group backed by Japanese and European ships conducted exercises near disputed features. China responded with the largest naval “encirclement” since 2016, including a carrier (美航母坐镇撑腰，美日欧三路轮番南海，26艘中国舰船“强势围观”).

  • Pentagon official calls U.S.-China military relations most stable in years – A senior U.S. defense official stated that current military-to-military engagement with China is at its strongest, even as Beijing arms Iran and conducts massive naval shows of force (五角大楼官员：目前的美中军事关系是近年来最为稳固的).

  • China conducts military AI research – The PLA’s military science academy is exploring “AI with Chinese characteristics” for warfare, signaling Beijing’s intent to lead in military artificial intelligence (走好中国特色人工智能创新发展之路).

  • Bohai Sea military exercise announced – A navigation warning for live-fire drills in the Bohai Sea adds to the growing list of PLA activities around China's periphery (航行警告！渤海部分海域进行军事演习 禁止驶入).

Signal: The PLA is at once projecting power in the South China Sea while expanding its hypersonic reach; the Pentagon’s “stable relations” remark may be an attempt to de-escalate, but the gap between words and actions is wide. Expect further drills and test launches in the coming week.

News Radar — 科技新闻

2026-07-30 · Window: 24h · Items: 101 · Generated: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

Editor's Brief

This morning's tech landscape is shaped by aggressive AI monetization pushes, a sweeping US robot import ban, and contrasting fortunes in electric vehicles. Qualcomm is raising chip prices, the FCC's ban now explicitly covers robot vacuums, and Ferrari's first EV sold out its 2026 allocation in weeks. Meanwhile, Microsoft and Meta are openly competing with OpenAI and Anthropic, and South Korea's AI bubble appears to have burst. In the developer community, a Vision Pro housing hack (ironically) and reflections on productivity dominate discussions.

  • Qualcomm's price hike hits smartphone processors starting Sept 1, compounding memory cost increases. Source
  • FCC's robot ban sweeps up robot vacuums, not just humanoids, as US government extends restrictions to Chinese-made advanced robotics. Source | Engadget
  • Ferrari Luce EV sells out ~500 units for 2026 in less than two months, defying design criticism. Source
  • Microsoft reports $3.2B profit from Anthropic investment, while OpenAI results are mixed; the company confirms a Copilot super app launching this year. Source | The Verge
  • Zuckerberg predicts billions will have personal AI agents within five years as Meta bets heavily on enterprise AI. Source
  • South Korea's AI bubble appears to have popped, with multiple video analyses and discussions on Hacker News. Source | Source 2
  • Post-quantum cryptography candidate HAWK is knocked out by a new Mythos attack that reveals years-hidden weaknesses. Source

Watch next: Monitor the fallout from the FCC robot ban on consumer robotics, Ford's 2028 robotaxi plans against Tesla's rival efforts, and the solid-state battery alliance between SK On and Factorial Energy. In AI, the US considering a FINRA-style watchdog for top models could reshape regulation.

科技产品 · 33 items

Consumer electronics saw several significant developments: Qualcomm announced processor price hikes from September 1st, the US government's robot import ban now explicitly covers robot vacuums (not just humanoids), and Winamp is attempting a comeback with a Deezer-powered service. Meanwhile, Google Play expands age confirmation tools globally, Xbox confirms game discs should have worked during its recent outage, and Apple's new Upgrade program is explained.

  • Qualcomm raising chip prices starting Sept 1, adding to 'RAMageddon' cost pressures. Source
  • US robot ban includes vacuums – FCC confirms Chinese-made robot vacuums, not just humanoids, are subject to new restrictions. Source | The Verge
  • Winamp revival aims to leverage nostalgia with a premium Deezer-powered player in a crowded streaming market. Source
  • Google Play's Age Signals API will expand globally by year-end to help developers verify user ages. Source
  • Cyberpunk 2077 is now a polished experience at a $20 discount, showcasing its transformation. Source

Signal: Expect higher smartphone prices this fall due to Qualcomm's move, and watch for how appliance retailers react to the vacuum ban.

The EV market saw a mix of luxury success and mainstream expansion. Ferrari's first EV, the Luce, sold out its 2026 allocation (about 500 units) in under two months despite design criticism. Hyundai's IONIQ 3 (starting at $30,000 with 300+ miles range) is generating record pre-order interest, while Waymo resumes freeway operations after a construction-related pause. Solid-state battery leaders SK On and Factorial Energy are joining forces to scale the technology.

  • Waymo returns to freeways after May pause due to construction zone incidents. Source
  • SK On + Factorial Energy alliance aims to scale solid-state EV batteries for mass production. Source

Signal: Affordable long-range EVs (Hyundai IONIQ 3) and luxury halo EVs (Ferrari Luce) are both finding demand, while solid-state battery partnerships signal a race to next-gen technology.

足球 · 20 条

今日足球新闻不多，但两条重磅信息值得关注。利物浦CEO Billy Hogan在纽约接受BBC专访，明确表示FSG正与多个财团进行投资谈判，强调“变革不可避免”，但不会完全出售俱乐部，这意味着红军可能迎来新股东但仍保留美资背景。另一边，国际足联正式对阿根廷国家队开启纪律处分程序，因世界杯决赛后球员与球迷冲突，以及比赛中展示福克兰群岛主权横幅，可能面临罚款或禁赛。

  • FIFA对阿根廷启动纪律处分，涉决赛后行为及政治标语

两件事均涉及顶级俱乐部的治理与国家队形象管理，后续发展将牵动球迷与投资者的神经。

News Radar — 体育新闻

2026-07-30 · Window: 24h · Items: 39 · Generated: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

Editor's Brief

Today's sports landscape is dominated by the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, a deepening cricket cheating scandal, and major football governance controversies. Meanwhile, Chinese basketball undergoes structural changes and the esports community reacts to LCK upsets.

  • Commonwealth Games highlights: Scottish swimmer Angharad Evans wins breaststroke gold, Northern Ireland's Kate O'Connor claims heptathlon gold, and England's netball team crushes Tonga 94-32.
  • Cricket scandal escalates: The Saltburn 'Clicky Ponting' affair sees player suspended as the club concedes the next match; analysis highlights the wicketkeeper's crucial role. Meanwhile, Sir Garfield Sobers is honored at his state funeral and Stephen Fleming is expected to become England Test coach.
  • Football governance and club news: FIFA opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina for post-World Cup behavior and a Falklands banner. Liverpool CEO Billy Hogan discusses FSG's transition and investment. Gianni Infantino's plan to sell World Cup stakes draws scrutiny.
  • Darts and boxing: Luke Littler's dominance questioned as most dominant sportsperson; Sebastian Bialecki wins Players Championship 26. Ugandan boxer Aziz Abdul, grandson of Idi Amin, disqualified for headbutt at Commonwealth Games.
  • Chinese basketball shifts: New CBA rules require college players to enter the draft before NBL. Former NBA player Alize Johnson joins Paris Basketball. Greg Oden recalls earning $1M in six months in CBA.
  • Esports community frenzy: LCK sees KT Rolster defeat T1 for the second time in a row, sparking fan outrage and calls for roster changes. BLG beats LGD in LPL. Steve Kerr addresses Warriors-James trade rumors.

Watch next: Keep an eye on the fallout from the Saltburn investigation, the Commonwealth Games medal race, the CBA draft rule implementation, and the LCK/LPL playoff implications as the season heats up.

足球 · 20 items

The 足球 desk captured a wide range of sports today, from Commonwealth Games heroics to cricket scandals and football governance issues. The Commonwealth Games delivered gold for Scottish swimmer Angharad Evans and Northern Irish heptathlete Kate O'Connor, while England's netball team dominated Tonga. Cricket controversies remain front-page news with the Saltburn 'Clicky Ponting' scandal leading to a player suspension and broader industry debate. In football, FIFA charged Argentina over post-World Cup behavior and a Falklands banner; Liverpool CEO Billy Hogan outlined FSG's transition plans; and Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off proposal stirred debate. Other notable stories: Stephen Fleming expected as England Test coach, Sir Garfield Sobers' state funeral, Luke Littler's darting dominance, and boxing disqualification at the Commonwealth Games.

This diverse mix of Olympic sports, cricket controversies, and football politics keeps the desk highly dynamic heading into the weekend.

多频道新闻雷达 — 娱乐新闻

2026-07-30 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 74 · 生成时间: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

板块速览

今日娱乐头条由BTS与格莱美的对峙引爆——防弹少年团宣布不参与2027年格莱美奖申报，以抗议新设“最佳亚洲流行表演”奖项，格莱美CEO Harvey Mason Jr.公开回应表示“伤心”但仍坚持该奖项“绝非分裂”12。与此同时，欧美票房迎来《蜘蛛侠：崭新一日》开画，目标冲击2026年最高首周纪录，Tom Holland透露早期剪辑版曾“令人讨厌”3。中国方面，微短剧产业领军人物王海歌被推至聚光灯下4，而微博社区则因“苏新皓全场红热搜”和“张泽禹被逼道歉”两起事件持续发酵56。日韩方面，fromis_9宣布亚洲巡演，ILLIT与LE SSERAFIM获日本白金认证7。

后续观察：BTS与格莱美的博弈可能重塑亚洲音乐人在国际奖项中的策略，格莱美新设分类的争议远未结束；《蜘蛛侠》票房表现将检验“超级英雄疲劳”是否真正被打破；微博上年轻偶像的舆论危机频发，反映出粉丝文化与公众道德期待之间的张力持续升级。

欧美 · 52 条

欧美板块今日重量级新闻密集。BTS抵制格莱美引发连锁反应，格莱美CEO Harvey Mason Jr.先后通过Rolling Stone和Deadline发声，表示“伤心但尊重决定”，并强调亚洲流行奖项“不是为了分裂”。Tom Holland自曝《蜘蛛侠：崭新一日》早期剪辑版令人“讨厌”，最终版成败将在本周末票房揭晓——该片目标瞄准2026年最高开画纪录。此外，Ben Affleck与Jeopardy冠军Jamie Ding联手赢得《百万富翁》100万美元奖金（捐给其刚果倡议基金会），延续去年Matt Damon的胜利。Tame Impala与Blackpink成员Jennie在波士顿首次现场合作《Dracula》，刷新舞台期待。

  • BTS不提交格莱美，CEO回应
  • Tom Holland透露蜘蛛侠早期剪辑版“令人讨厌”
  • Ben Affleck赢得《谁想成为百万富翁》100万美元
  • Tame Impala与Jennie首次现场合作《Dracula》
  • Fox Fighters北美巡演启动

中国娱乐产业今日聚焦于微短剧的资本化与国际传播。王海歌被视为“中国微短剧短片产业开拓者”，引发行业对其商业模式和内容质量的双重讨论。与此同时，中非情缘第六季影视展播在内罗毕启动，影视旅游成为新热点——有分析提出从内容创作、目的地开发到产业链协同“三个维度”发力。电通发布《真诚，自有引力》体育娱乐趋势2.0报告，直击中国文娱体育生态。此外，A股影视传媒板块获得北向资金加仓，外资机构密集调研，显示对中国娱乐市场信心回升。杨幂历年电视剧被盘点，虽为题外话，但反映出其长尾关注度。

item.content:encoded:
News Radar — 娱乐新闻

2026-07-30 · Window: 24h · Items: 74 · Generated: 2026-07-30 04:20 UTC

Editor's Brief

The entertainment landscape today is dominated by a major industry rift as BTS boycotts the 2027 Grammys over the new Asian Pop category, while Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' aims for a record-breaking box office weekend. In a cultural firestorm, author Joyce Carol Oates defended Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' against a scathing translator review, and Ben Affleck won $1M for charity on 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire.' Meanwhile, K-pop crossovers and Korean content expansion signal shifting global dynamics.

  • Grammys vs. BTS: A Crossroads for Asian Representation: BTS announced they will not submit for the 2027 Grammys, protesting the new 'Best Asian Pop Music Performance' category as divisive. Grammy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. expressed being 'saddened' but defended the category as 'never to divide' (Deadline, Rolling Stone). This moves beyond a single award to questions about how Western institutions recognize non-Western music.
  • Spider-Man Aims to Break 2026's Box Office Ceiling: Sony's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' targets the year's biggest opening, with analysts calling it a 'gold standard' for superhero relevance (The Hollywood Reporter). Tom Holland revealed he 'hated' an early cut of the film, underscoring the creative struggles behind blockbuster success (Deadline).
  • Literary Feud: Joyce Carol Oates vs. Translator Emily Wilson: Oates slammed Wilson's viral review of Nolan's 'The Odyssey' as 'crude language of MAGA folks,' igniting a debate over scholarly critique versus cultural gatekeeping (Variety). The clash highlights tensions between classicists and popular filmmakers.
  • Ben Affleck's Charity Million: Affleck, alongside Jeopardy champ Jamie Ding, won $1M on 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire' for his Eastern Congo Initiative, following Matt Damon's win last year (Variety). Celebrity game show philanthropy continues to drive major donations.
  • Disney+ Korea Doubles Down on Fortune-Telling Reality: After 'Battle of Fates' became Disney+ Korea's biggest series premiere, a spinoff 'House of Fates' has been greenlit, sending guests on spiritual pilgrimages (Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter). This signals streaming platforms' appetite for localized, supernatural content.
  • K-Pop Crossover: Tame Impala & Jennie Perform 'Dracula' Live: For the first time, the Australian band and BLACKPINK's Jennie performed their hit together in Boston, marking a significant moment in Western-K-pop collaboration (Rolling Stone).
  • Chinese Entertainment Trends: Micro-Short Dramas and Market Inflows: Wang Haige is highlighted as a pioneer in China's micro-short drama sector (中华网), while foreign capital is pouring into Chinese entertainment companies, per Sina Finance (新浪网).
  • Weibo Drama: Su Xinhao's Concert Fans Chant for 'Hot Search' and Zhang Zeyu Apology Controversy: Su Xinhao's concert fans orchestrated a 'full red' trending topic, while Zhang Zeyu faced backlash with 'victim-blaming' discourse (微博社区动态). These stories reveal the power of organized fanbases and the rapid spread of online discourse.

Watch next: The BTS-Grammys fallout will likely dominate music industry conversations, especially if other Asian artists follow suit. Spider-Man's opening weekend numbers will be closely tracked as a bellwether for superhero fatigue. On the Chinese front, the micro-short drama regulation and foreign investment trends bear watching. Weibo's trending mechanisms continue to shape celebrity narratives, with potential for regulatory scrutiny.

欧美 · 52 items

The Western entertainment desk is buzzing with the Grammys-BTS standoff, Spider-Man's box office ambitions, and Ben Affleck's game show win. A literary spat over 'The Odyssey' adaptation and a new Korean reality spinoff on Disney+ also command attention.

  • Grammys CEO 'Saddened' by BTS Withdrawal, Defends Asian Pop Category: Harvey Mason Jr. responded to BTS's boycott after the new category was added, calling it a move to 'celebrate' rather than divide. The decision could reshape how the Academy engages with global pop (Deadline, Hollywood Reporter).
  • Spider-Man: Brand New Day Targets Record Opening: The film aims to be the highest-grossing domestic opening of 2026, potentially calming fears of superhero fatigue. Tom Holland's admission of a hated early cut adds behind-the-scenes drama (Hollywood Reporter, Deadline).
  • Ben Affleck Wins $1M for Charity on 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire': The actor's win for his Eastern Congo Initiative continues a trend of celebrities leveraging game shows for philanthropy. Matt Damon won the same prize last year (Variety).
  • Joyce Carol Oates Defends Nolan's 'The Odyssey': Oates' fiery rebuttal to translator Emily Wilson's negative review underscores deep cultural divisions over adaptation faithfulness (Variety).
  • Disney+ Korea Greenlights 'House of Fates': The spinoff of the record-breaking 'Battle of Fates' will send guests on fortune-telling tours across Korea, hosted by the original show's top readers (Deadline).

BTS's Grammy boycott and Spider-Man's box office performance are the two key signals to watch in the coming days for their impact on the broader entertainment industry.

多频道新闻雷达 — 经济新闻

2026-07-29 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 125 · 生成时间: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

板块速览

7月29日经济新闻速览

全球市场在AI抛售与中东冲突双重夹击下剧烈波动。亚洲科技股延续跌势，SK海力士因盈利不及预期暴跌，SoftBank重挫10%，但港股腾讯、美团等逆势上涨。伊朗向美军发射弹道导弹，油价应声跳涨，惠誉报告警告战争溢出效应已拖累欧洲发达经济体。苹果成为史上第二家市值突破5万亿美元的公司，因投资者逃离AI股转向硬件龙头。国内A股存储芯片板块暴跌超6%，2400亿市值兆易创新跌停，但光模块巨头中际旭创董事长提议最高80亿元回购，ETF资金昨日整体净流入253亿元。

  • 亚洲科技股抛售延续，SK海力士盈利超预期仍遭抛售：SK海力士利润与营收呈指数级增长，但未达到AI板块分析师过高预期，股价暴跌。软银重挫10%，港股中国互联网股逆势走强，腾讯、美团、百度、快手均上涨。
  • 伊朗突袭美军基地，油价飙升：伊朗向中东美军发射弹道导弹，所有导弹被拦截，但中东紧张局势再度升级，油价大幅上涨。沙特正通过地中海港口以更高成本出口石油寻求替代路线。
  • 苹果突破5万亿美元市值：投资者逃离AI和半导体板块，苹果受益于强劲产品需求和避开AI军备竞赛的决策，股价创历史新高，成为继英伟达后第二家市值超5万亿美元的公司。
  • A股存储芯片板块暴跌，光模块龙头大手笔回购：受全球AI芯片抛售波及，A股存储芯片指数跳水超6%，兆易创新跌停；但光模块巨头中际旭创董事长提议回购最高80亿元，彰显信心。
  • 韩国交易所启动熔断机制：韩国KOSPI指数跌至三个月新低，三星和SK海力士跌幅均超10%，交易所触发熔断，AI支出担忧与中国芯片竞争双重打击。
  • 美联储公布货币政策工作组领导层与目标：美联储宣布成立两个工作组推进货币政策实施，同时发布银行检查中敏感信息处理联合声明，显示监管层正多维度强化金融体系韧性。

后续观察：AI板块的“盈利疲劳”正从韩国、日本蔓延至全球，英伟达、谷歌等巨头财报后的资本支出审查将成为本周焦点。中东冲突若持续升级，油价和通胀预期可能迫使央行重新评估降息路径。中国科技股在AI抛售中展现韧性，需关注周末公布的PMI数据能否巩固这一分化趋势。

美股 · 62 条

美股市场整体承压，AI板块抛售潮未止，但苹果、福特等个别公司凭借业绩或差异化策略逆势上涨。中东战事推高油价，能源股走强；监管层动作频频，美联储推进内部改革，特朗普法律案及马斯克旗下xAI诉讼亦引发关注。

  • SK海力士盈利翻倍仍遭抛售，AI期望过高成风险：收入与利润翻倍增长，但未能满足华尔街对AI宠儿的极致预期，股价暴跌，拖累整个半导体板块。
  • 苹果成第二家5万亿美元公司，投资者逃离AI涌入硬件：苹果凭借对AI军备竞赛的克制和产品涨价能力，吸引避险资金，市值突破5万亿美元。
  • 福特上调全年指引，Q2盈利超预期：福特受益于运营改善、定价韧性和高利润产品组合，宣布F系列卡车复苏计划进展顺利，股价盘后上涨。
  • 伊朗导弹袭击致油价飙升，能源板块震荡：伊朗突袭美军基地后，布伦特原油大幅上涨，沙特寻找替代出口路线，市场对供应中断的担忧升温。
  • 亚马逊、Meta、微软本周围绕资本支出面临投资者拷问：谷歌财报显示自由现金流转负并提升资本支出，引发市场对超大规模云厂商回报率的担忧，投资者将密切关注本周科技巨头的财报电话会。

判断：AI交易正在经历去泡沫化的阵痛，但苹果、福特等非AI核心公司的强劲表现显示市场并非全面崩溃。中东地缘风险是短期最大变量，油价走势将直接影响通胀预期和联储政策。

中国经济 · 34 条

中国资产在全球AI抛售中展现相对韧性，港股互联网逆市上涨，渣打银行利润创新高并启动回购。但A股存储芯片板块受海外冲击严重，光模块龙头以回购稳定信心。人民币国际化与香港经济前景成为关注焦点。

  • 港股互联网逆势走高，腾讯、美团等领涨：亚洲科技股普遍下跌，但香港上市中国互联网股票（腾讯、美团、百度、快手）全部上涨，显示资金从AI芯片转向消费互联网板块。
  • 渣打银行上半年利润增10%，启动10亿美元回购：净利创纪录达33.7亿美元，但中东冲突导致的减值损失抵消了财富管理收益，回购计划表明管理层对资本实力有信心。
  • A股存储芯片暴跌6%，光模块巨头提议80亿元回购：受海外AI芯片抛售传染，兆易创新跌停，但中际旭创董事长提议回购，释放低位信心信号。ETF资金昨日净流入253亿元，显示机构借机抄底。
  • 上海清算所推动离岸人民币扩张，瞄准全球增长：上清所所长马建阳撰文称将通过全球金融网络扩大离岸人民币池，巩固上海在衍生品清算中的主导地位，同时隔离国内风险。
  • 香港房价连涨13个月但涨幅放缓：6月香港楼价继续上涨，但增速放缓至13个月来最低，高利率与地缘风险制约购买力。

判断：中国资产正从AI泡沫中分离，互联网、银行等传统板块成为避风港。人民币国际化提速和香港经济结构调整（AI出口拉动）是中长期主线，但短期仍需观察海外科技股抛售对A股情绪的溢出效应。

item.content:encoded:
News Radar — 经济新闻

2026-07-29 · Window: 24h · Items: 125 · Generated: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

Editor's Brief

Markets were buffeted by a deepening rout in AI-related stocks and a renewed spike in geopolitical risk after Iran launched a ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces, sending oil sharply higher. Chinese internet stocks listed in Hong Kong provided a rare bright spot, while Apple crossed the $5tn mark as investors rotated away from high-spending AI plays. In Europe, earnings reports offered some support, but the Iran conflict’s spillovers into developed economies remain a key risk. The next 24 hours bring crucial hyperscaler earnings from Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft, as well as the Eurozone GDP flash estimate, which will test the resilience of risk appetite.

  • AI rout intensifies across Asia: SK Hynix shares tanked after exponential earnings growth failed to meet AI-inflated expectations, dragging SoftBank down 10% and triggering South Korea's KOSPI circuit breaker. However, Seagate's after-hours earnings beat offered a glimmer of hope for the battered AI trade (CNBC, MarketWatch).
  • Iran attack jolts oil markets: Iran launched a ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces, all intercepted, but oil prices jumped sharply as the U.S.-Iran cycle of strikes resumed (CNBC). Saudi Arabia is using a costlier Mediterranean backdoor to keep exports flowing (MarketWatch).
  • Apple hits $5tn as investors flee AI stocks: Apple became the second company ever to reach a $5tn valuation, benefiting from strong product demand and its decision to sit out the AI spending race (Guardian).
  • Chinese internet stocks buck the sell-off: Tencent, Meituan, Baidu, and Kuaishou all traded higher in Hong Kong, diverging from the regional AI-driven weakness (CNBC).
  • U.S. bans Chinese humanoid robots: The Trump administration escalated tech tensions with a ban on Chinese humanoid robots, intensifying the U.S.-China race for leadership in robotics and AI (BBC).
  • Ford raises guidance after Q2 beat: Ford cited operational improvements, resilient pricing, and strong F-Series mix for the positive outlook (CNBC).
  • Standard Chartered posts record profit, $1bn buyback: The London-headquartered lender’s first-half net profit rose 10% to a record $3.37bn, though an impairment charge tied to the Middle East conflict weighed (SCMP).
  • Europe feels the heat from Iran war: Fitch warned that Iran war spillovers are straining developed Europe’s economy in 2026 (IndexBox).

Watch next: Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft report this week under intense scrutiny over capital spending and free cash flow after Alphabet’s disappointing results. Eurozone Q2 GDP flash estimate on Thursday will be critical for ECB’s September rate decision. In Asia, the trajectory of Chinese AI stocks and any further chip-related fallout will set the tone.

美股 · 62 items

U.S. equities face a tug-of-war between a deepening AI rout and bright spots in energy and industrial earnings. Apple’s $5tn milestone underscores a defensive rotation away from high-capex AI names, while Iran’s missile attack drove oil higher and revived geopolitical risk premiums. Ford’s earnings beat and raised guidance provided a lift for the auto sector, but the hyperscaler earnings season remains the dominant near-term catalyst.

  • The AI sell-off spread to Asian tech bellwethers SK Hynix and SoftBank, but U.S. traders are bracing for similar scrutiny on Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft after Alphabet’s free cash flow turned negative (CNBC).
  • Apple hit a $5.04tn market cap as investors sought safety, partly because Apple is sitting out the AI spending race (Guardian).
  • Oil jumped on renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities, with Brent and WTI spiking after Iran’s ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces (CNBC).
  • Ford raised its full-year guidance after a Q2 earnings beat, citing operational improvements and resilient F-Series demand (CNBC).
  • Seagate’s earnings beat provided a rare bright spot for the AI trade in after-hours trading (MarketWatch).

Signal: Watch for further rotation out of AI hype into value and energy, but the hyperscaler reports this week will determine if the sell-off is a correction or a structural shift.

中国经济 · 34 items

Chinese markets saw a split between resilient Hong Kong-listed internet stocks and a sharp sell-off in A-share chip names, as the global AI rout hit local sentiment. Meanwhile, financial infrastructure and wealth management flows suggest medium-term confidence in China’s offshore yuan push and Hong Kong’s role. The day’s news also highlighted continued corporate real estate moves and robotics diversification.

  • Standard Chartered reported a 10% profit rise to a record $3.37bn and announced a $1bn buyback, though a Middle East impairment charge weighed; the results underscore China-linked bank resilience (SCMP).
  • Shanghai Clearing House is pushing an expanded offshore yuan model to boost international bond sales, aiming to solidify Shanghai’s derivatives clearing dominance (SCMP).
  • A-share storage chip stocks plunged over 6%, with 240-billion-yuan GigaDevice hitting limit-down, reflecting global AI sector contagion (同花顺).
  • Hong Kong home prices extended gains for a 13th month in June, though the pace slowed, supporting property-linked stocks (Reuters).
  • HSBC is relocating its group chief people officer from London to Hong Kong, doubling down on its Asia pivot (SCMP).

Signal: The resilience of Hong Kong-listed Chinese internet stocks amid the AI rout is a key divergence to watch; if sustained, it could signal decoupling from the U.S. tech cycle.

欧洲经济 · 23 items

European equities edged higher supported by robust corporate earnings, but the macroeconomic backdrop is clouded by the Iran conflict and its spillover effects on trade and energy. The ECB is preparing for a potential September rate hike, with the flash Q2 GDP reading critical. Consumer goods giant Unilever warned of further price increases, adding to inflation concerns.

  • Fitch released a report warning that Iran war spillovers are straining developed Europe’s economy in 2026, highlighting supply chain and energy cost risks (IndexBox).
  • Unilever warned it will push through further price rises over coming months to offset rising costs, though strong World Cup marketing boosted sales in Q2 (Guardian).
  • European stocks ended modestly higher as strong corporate earnings offset interest rate concerns; the DAX, CAC, and FTSE 100 all edged up (Yahoo Finance UK).
  • The ECB extended the use of climate factors in its collateral framework to non-financial corporate credit claims, a step toward greening monetary policy (ECB).
  • European real estate markets continue a stable recovery, with investors adopting a more selective approach, according to Cushman & Wakefield (Google News).

Signal: Thursday’s Eurozone GDP flash will be pivotal; weaker-than-expected growth could tilt the ECB toward a hold, while strong data would keep a September hike firmly on the table.

板块速览

今日社会新闻综述

全球社会新闻今日多线并发：中东战火再起，伊朗向驻约旦美军发射弹道导弹，打破五天停火期；日本九州岛遭遇6.8级强震，死亡人数已升至13人，搜救仍在紧张进行；韩国股市因芯片股崩盘暴跌近11%，触发熔断，恐慌情绪蔓延；美国西雅图美食节枪击案致三人死亡，社区举行悼念。此外，法国野火因热浪复燃，墨西哥贩毒集团将冰毒实验室外包至尼日利亚，以及日本著名作家东野圭吾去世等消息也引发关注。

  • 中东再燃战火：伊朗向驻约旦美军发射多枚弹道导弹，美军中央司令部称成功拦截。此前双方刚经历五天停火，局势骤然升级。（BBC、Al Jazeera）

News Radar — 社会新闻

2026-07-29 · Window: 24h · Items: 87 · Generated: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

Editor's Brief

The last 24 hours have been dominated by a sharp escalation in US-Iran hostilities, a devastating earthquake in southern Japan, and a severe sell-off in South Korean equities, while domestic Chinese news focused on policy and social stability. The re-emergence of direct Iran-US military exchanges after a five-day pause risks a broader regional war, and the magnitude 7 earthquake on Kyushu island has already claimed lives and disrupted critical infrastructure. Meanwhile, South Korea's KOSPI plunge of nearly 11%—triggered by panic selling of chipmakers—signals deepening anxiety over the global AI memory cycle. Below are the key developments you need to track.

  • Iran and US trade strikes, shattering brief lull in fighting – US Central Command confirms interception of multiple Iranian ballistic missiles targeting US forces in Jordan, ending a five-day pause. The Al Jazeera report notes Riyadh and Washington also launched joint strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq, widening the theater of conflict.
  • Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing – At least 13 dead, hundreds injured, and tens of thousands without power and water after a 6.8 magnitude quake struck Kyushu. A blast at a Kumamoto mall and building collapses complicate rescue efforts; military has mobilized thousands. (See also BBC video and Reuters report)
  • South Korea's Kospi share index falls nearly 7% – Heavy selling of chipmakers drove the KOSPI down nearly 11% at one point, triggering circuit breakers. The rout followed SK hynix's record profit report, suggesting the market is pricing in a peak in AI memory demand.
  • Netanyahu to meet Trump in a first encounter since the Iran war began – Both leaders face domestic pressures: Netanyahu's re-election campaign and Trump's unpopular war. The meeting could reshape US-Israel coordination on Iran.
  • Wildfires in south-west France flare up as region braces for new 40C heatwave – Firefighters in Gironde face a sharp temperature rise complicating containment efforts—a reminder of accelerating climate extremes.
  • China's tax big data shows H1 economic highlights – Official data signals steady recovery; watch for implications for policy easing.

Watch next: The Iran-US missile exchange could escalate further if retaliatory strikes target Iranian soil. Japan's earthquake rescue operations are in a critical 72-hour window, while South Korea's market rout may prompt emergency policy measures. Also keep an eye on the Netanyahu-Trump summit for signs of a shift in war strategy.

欧美 · 39 items

The desk was dominated by renewed military confrontation between Iran and the US, with Iranian ballistic missiles targeting US forces in Jordan after a five-day lull. US Central Command confirmed successful interceptions, but the attacks signal Tehran's willingness to test Washington's defenses. In parallel, joint US-Saudi strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq widen the conflict geography. Meanwhile, notable developments include Netanyahu's upcoming meeting with Trump, a fatal shooting at a Seattle food festival, and the ongoing fallout from the Idaho student murders trial.

  • Iran and US trade strikes and US forces in Jordan targeted – The end of a brief pause in Iran-US hostilities. Al Jazeera and BBC both report the strikes; implications for broader Middle East stability are severe.
  • Netanyahu to meet Trump – The first face-to-face since the Iran war began. Both leaders have political incentives to project strength; expect decisions on escalatory or de-escalatory steps.
  • US walks out of UN Security Council meeting – A diplomatic row after the US joined North Korea and Russia in opposing extension of the UN human rights chief's term; this isolates Washington further on multilateral platforms.
  • Seattle food festival shooting – Three killed; community mourning. The incident underscores ongoing gun violence in the US.
  • Wildfires in France – A new 40°C heatwave threatens to reignite efforts in Gironde, highlighting climate risks.

The key signal to watch: whether the Iran missile strike is a one-off or the start of a sustained campaign. Escalation could draw in Gulf states and affect oil markets.

Rescue operations are ongoing amid building collapses and a mall explosion. In financial markets, South Korea's KOSPI plunged nearly 11% in a single session, triggering circuit breakers, as investors dumped chipmaker shares—including SK hynix despite its record Q2 profit—over fears of peaking AI memory demand.

  • South Korea's Kospi sinks nearly 11% – Heavy selling of chipmakers, including SK hynix, which earlier reported record Q2 profit. The crash suggests the market is pricing in a downturn in AI memory after the recent boom.
  • AI cameras spot suicide attempts in Seoul – A notable social technology deployment: AI cameras in the capital detect suicide attempts, raising privacy and effectiveness debates.
  • ICC president seeks Japan's aid to counter Trump push – Geopolitical undercurrent: International Criminal Court asks Tokyo to resist Washington's pressure on Asian member withdrawals.

The Japan earthquake could disrupt semiconductor supply lines; the KOSPI crash may force BOK or government intervention. Both stories have immediate cross-border economic consequences.

多频道新闻雷达 — 军事新闻

2026-07-29 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 60 · 生成时间: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

板块速览

军事新闻日报 · 2026-07-29

导语： 24小时内，中东局势急剧升级——伊朗向美军发起弹道导弹突袭，美军防空库存被指接近极限；同时乌克兰与伊朗冲突在里海交汇，两场战争正加速融合。美国暂停对伊打击后，转而强化印太布局，中国则在台海与南海持续施压。以下是关键动态与判断。

  • 伊朗突袭美军，防空库存告急：伊朗于7月28日向驻中东美军发射多枚弹道导弹，美国军方定性为“企图突袭”。WSJ和BBC等多家媒体确认。分析指出，美军“爱国者”等防空弹药库存因长期消耗已近临界点，Sun Sentinel援引报告称库存承压。
  • 乌克兰与伊朗冲突在里海交叉：乌克兰对一艘伊朗船只发动袭击，造成一名伊朗水兵死亡，伊朗威胁报复。NYT与Newsweek指出，乌克兰与伊朗战争正“融合”为同一危机，特朗普政府被迫同时应对两条战线。
  • 特朗普暂停打击，但威胁持续：特朗普称与伊朗的“会谈良好”，同时重申打击威胁；The Guardian评论认为，暂停本身暴露美军力量有限。美海军航母动态显示，对伊打击虽暂停，但海上封锁未解除。TWZ
  • 中国军力展示与南海博弈：解放军在渤海海峡及黄海部分海域执行军事任务；直升机与无人机首次同时越过台海中线进入管控区域。朝鲜日报美国智库报告则聚焦中国核武库增长。TWZ
  • 印太：美强化菲律宾基地，中俄联合巡逻：美国承诺资助菲律宾海岸警卫队扩建巴拉望基地，并增加军事融资。USNI中俄海军在日本北海道附近举行年度联合巡逻，日方侦察确认。USNI国会同时要求海军大幅增加鱼雷库存以支撑“两场战争”战略。Naval News
  • 美军装备战线：最后一架MV-22“鱼鹰”交付海军陆战队，预计服役至2055年。TWZ而“企业”号航母报废账单已达13亿美元。USNI此外，波音在“空军一号”项目上已额外承担30亿美元超支。TWZ

后续观察： 伊朗突袭与乌克兰行动的联动，很可能迫使美国重新评估中东兵力部署。中国在台海与南海军力展示持续，美国虽暂停对伊打击，但印太方向投入不减。美伊外交窗口期极短，一旦破裂将引爆更大范围冲突。

概览： 过去24小时，国际安全焦点集中在伊朗对美军的导弹突袭、美国防空库存告急以及美军与阿联酋成立首个AI联合任务组。以下为关键研判：

  • 伊朗突袭美军，库存承压： 伊朗发射弹道导弹攻击中东美军，WSJ与BBC均有报道。分析Sun Sentinel指出关键防空弹药库存已接近极限。
  • 美韩防空演练与阿联酋AI合作： 美韩完成第7届联合防空导弹学院课程，pacaf.af.mil美军中央司令部与阿联酋成立“Talon Synapse”AI联合任务组，DefenseScoop标志美军加速在盟友中推广AI作战能力。
  • 美军伤员记录与航母态势： 新解密的记录显示美军在伊朗冲突中遭受弹片、骨折和头部创伤等伤情，Stars and Stripes美航母位置报告TWZ显示海上封锁未松动。

收束： 伊朗突袭暴露美军防空弹药短板，阿联酋AI合作则显示美国积极寻求技术联盟弥补兵力漏洞。

2026-07-29 · Window: 24h · Items: 60 · Generated: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

Editor's Brief

The last 24 hours have been defined by a dramatic escalation in the Middle East, as Iran launched a surprise missile attack against U.S. forces, triggering a rapid reassessment of American force posture and air defense stockpiles. Simultaneously, a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea is blurring the lines between two major conflicts, while China continues to assert itself in the South China Sea and Taiwan Strait. This brief synthesizes the most consequential developments across four desks—international security, conflict dynamics, China military affairs, and naval/Indo-Pacific operations—to provide actionable intelligence.

  • Iran launches 'attempted surprise attack' on U.S. forces: Multiple ballistic missiles were fired at American troops and air defense positions, with the U.S. military confirming the strike. Reports indicate air defense stockpiles are nearing limits, raising concerns about sustainability (WSJ, BBC, PBS).
  • Ukraine-Iran wars collide: Ukraine struck an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea, killing one sailor and prompting Iranian threats of retaliation. This incident, combined with the U.S.-Iran exchange, is merging two conflict theaters (NYT, Newsweek).
  • China expands military activities: Chinese helicopters and drones crossed the Taiwan Strait median line for the first time simultaneously, while a joint Russia-China naval patrol sailed near Japan. Beijing also issued a navigation warning for live-fire drills in the Bohai and Yellow Seas (朝鮮日報中文版, USNI).
  • U.S. air defense stockpiles under strain after recent fighting with Iran, with analysis warning of depleted inventories. The Pentagon may face hard choices on resupply (Sun Sentinel).
  • Trump meets Netanyahu and Zelenskyy separately at the White House, signaling diplomatic efforts to manage the cascading crises. Trump cited 'good' talks on Iran but reiterated strike threats (ABC13, Express Tribune).
  • U.S. Navy force posture reshuffling: The prized Ohio-class submarine USS Georgia is heading into retirement, while the carrier strike campaign against Iran is paused but the naval blockade continues. Congress also directed a torpedo inventory overhaul for a two-war strategy (TWZ, Naval News).
  • China's long-range nuclear missile arsenal continues to grow, as detailed in a new guide. Combined with the PLA report to Congress, this underscores the strategic competition (TWZ, USNI).

Watch next: The aftermath of Iran's missile attack will dominate headlines, with potential U.S. retaliatory strikes or diplomatic off-ramps. The merging of the Ukraine and Iran conflicts via the Caspian strike could widen the theater. China's trans-Median line incursions and South China Sea base expansion will keep the Indo-Pacific on edge. Monitor U.S. air defense stockpile replenishment decisions and any movement of carrier strike groups.

国际安全 · 31 items

The 国际安全 desk is dominated by Iran's surprise ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces in the Middle East, which has drawn down critical air defense stockpiles and forced the U.S. military to reassess its posture. Other major developments include the retirement of the Ohio-class submarine USS Georgia, the U.S.-South Korea air and missile defense academy, and new bilateral AI task forces.

  • Iran Launches Surprise Missile Attack on U.S. Forces: Multiple ballistic missiles targeted American troops; Pentagon confirms.
  • Air defense stockpiles near limit: Analysis warns stockpiles are critically low after recent engagements.
  • USS Georgia heading into retirement: All Ohio-class submarines to be retired within three years, impacting strike capability.
  • US-UAE AI task force formed: Task Force Talon Synapse aims to boost military AI applications in CENTCOM.
  • US troops wounded in Iran war documented: New records reveal shrapnel, broken bones, and head trauma from the conflict. Signal: The U.S. is simultaneously facing a fresh Iranian attack, depleted munitions, and the looming loss of a key submarine platform—this convergence will test the Pentagon's ability to sustain operations across theaters.

冲突局势 · 12 items

The 冲突局势 desk highlights the merging of the Ukraine and Iran wars, with a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea killing one sailor and threatening retaliation. Meanwhile, President Trump met separately with Netanyahu and Zelenskyy, citing 'good' talks on Iran while reiterating threats. Analysts suggest the conflict is spreading beyond its original boundaries.

  • Ukraine strikes Iranian ship in Caspian Sea: Iran condemns the attack, threatens retaliation, further linking the two theaters.
  • Trump meets Netanyahu and Zelenskyy: White House diplomacy aimed at managing overlapping crises.
  • Iran war spreading analysis: Multiple outlets note the widening scope of the conflict.
  • China seeking Red Sea pathway: Reports suggest Beijing is exploring its own maritime corridor, adding a new dimension.
  • Blurred front lines: Ukraine and Iran wars collide: CNBC analyzes the diplomatic and military entanglement. Signal: The Ukrainian strike on an Iranian vessel is a dangerous escalatory step that could force Washington to manage a two-front crisis, with the Red Sea and Horn of Africa emerging as potential flashpoints.

中国军情 · 10 items

China’s military assertiveness continues to rise, with multiple incidents in the past 24 hours: a navigation warning for live-fire drills in the Bohai and Yellow Seas, Chinese aircraft crossing the Taiwan Strait median line, and a marked increase in PLA activity near Japan. The U.S. added more Chinese firms to its 'China Military Companies List,' while Beijing blacklisted a Polish university—an unprecedented move. A new report details China's growing long-range nuclear arsenal.

  • Chinese aircraft cross Taiwan Strait median line: Helicopters and drones entered the restricted zone simultaneously for the first time.
  • Bohai and Yellow Sea military drills: China issues navigation warning, prohibiting vessel entry, likely for anti-ship or anti-air exercises.
  • China blacklists Polish university: Unprecedented move signals Beijing's willingness to use sanctions in academic/tech disputes.
  • U.S. adds Chinese firms to military list: Commerce Ministry responds, escalating tech rivalry.
  • China's nuclear missile arsenal detailed: A comprehensive guide shows expanding ICBM and SLBM capabilities, reinforcing strategic deterrence.
  • Desert target resembling Taipei Presidential Office: Experts warn of mock-up for strike training, signaling intent against Taiwan. Signal: China is simultaneously testing Taiwan’s airspace, expanding its nuclear arsenal, and imposing new sanctions—signaling a hardening stance that will complicate any U.S. effort to focus on the Middle East.

海军与印太 · 7 items

In the Indo-Pacific, the U.S. announced funding for a Philippine Coast Guard base expansion on Palawan, directly supporting South China Sea operations. A joint Russia-China naval patrol sailed near Japan, while the U.S. Congress directed a torpedo inventory overhaul to prepare for two major regional conflicts. Additionally, Poland’s A26 submarine deal and the scrapping of USS Enterprise highlight global naval modernization and decommissioning trends.

  • U.S. funds Philippine Coast Guard base: Up to $9 million for pier expansion on Palawan to enhance maritime law enforcement presence.
  • Russia-China joint patrol near Japan: PLAN cruiser, destroyer, and oiler operating with Russian corvette south of Hokkaido; annual patrol indicates deepening coordination.
  • Congress mandates torpedo inventory review for two-war strategy: FY27 NDAA requires SECNAV to overhaul torpedo production to support simultaneous major conflicts.
  • Poland orders A26 submarines: Three Swedish-built Blekinge-class boats with interim lease of HMS Södermanland; delivery by 2031.
  • USS Enterprise scrapping costs $1.3B: Final cost for recycling the first nuclear carrier underscores the expense of nuclear decommissioning.
  • HII expands distributed shipbuilding to amphibious ships: Modular construction begins for LPD 32 Philadelphia, building on destroyer program success. Signal: The U.S. is reinforcing its ally network in the South China Sea while preparing for a two-war scenario, but the retirement of key platforms like the USS Georgia and the high cost of decommissioning may strain resources exactly when they are most needed.

多频道新闻雷达 — 科技新闻

2026-07-29 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 104 · 生成时间: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

板块速览

今日科技新闻呈现多重震荡：AI领域遭遇股市恐慌与安全信任危机，芯片股因投资者对AI回报的担忧而集体下滑，同时OpenAI遭遇的黑客攻击被MIT Technology Review评价为“可预见的”。超过1100名AI专家联名呼吁暂停前沿AI开发，而Andrew Ng的LearnVector却逆势上线，试图用AI重塑个性化学习。科技产品方面，美国FCC宣布禁止进口外国制造的人形机器人和电源逆变器，矛头直指中国；eBay为2019年血腥猪面具骚扰案支付5600万美元和解金，成为企业治理反面教材。汽车圈则冷暖不均：沙特王子5%持股令Lucid股价飙升25%，但特斯拉前经理指控FSD测试车是“滚动隐患”，百度Apollo Go同日登陆伦敦街头。社区动态中，经典游戏《半条命》被移植到Mac OS 9引发怀旧热潮，而Manim动画引擎的浏览器化则展示了WebGPU的潜力。

  • 芯片股在美亚两地因AI焦虑重挫，投资者对AI资本支出的可持续性产生怀疑。
  • OpenAI遭“可预见的”黑客攻击，MIT Tech Review指出类似攻击早有先例。
  • 1100+AI专家呼吁全球放缓前沿AI研发，安全恐慌后监管呼声再起。
  • 美国禁止进口外国制造的人形机器人和电源逆变器，旨在推动国内新兴技术生产。
  • eBay及前高管以5600万美元和解网络跟踪案，涉及活昆虫、血腥猪面具等骇人手段。
  • 沙特王子Alwaleed披露5%持股，Lucid股价飙涨25%，为资金紧张的电动汽车制造商注入强心针。
  • 特斯拉FSD测试经理指控车辆为“滚动隐患”，新诉讼揭露安全员严重不足。
  • 《半条命》被移植到Mac OS 9，在Hacker News上获得186点热度，引发经典系统复兴讨论。

后续观察： 今日新闻的底层暗线是“信任危机”——无论是市场对AI投资回报的不信任、监管层对AI安全的不信任、还是公众对自动驾驶与大型科技企业行为的不信任。下周需关注芯片股能否企稳、FCC机器人禁令的后续影响，以及OpenAI是否会公布更详细的安全整改措施。

AI · 34 条

AI领域今日剧烈震荡。芯片股因投资者对AI资本开支回报的质疑而普跌（BBC）。安全层面，OpenAI最近遭遇的“前所未有”攻击被MIT Tech Review定性为“可预见的”，因为类似模式早已出现（MIT Technology Review）。与此同时，超过1100名AI专家联合呼吁全球暂停前沿AI开发（KuCoin），OpenAI和Anthropic员工也在推动加强监管（Chosunbiz）。在正面消息中，Andrew Ng的AI公司LearnVector推出个性化一对一学习体验（Hacker News），获85点社区关注。总体而言，AI行业正经历“技术乐观主义”与“安全现实主义”的激烈碰撞，短期内监管预期将持续压制估值。

科技产品 · 40 条

科技产品板块政策与法律事件密集。美国FCC宣布禁止进口外国制造的人形机器人和电源逆变器，明确针对中国，旨在重振国内制造（Engadget）。法律方面，eBay及三名前高管就2019年针对一对记者夫妇的恶性网络跟踪案支付5570万美元和解金，内容包括送活昆虫、血腥猪面具等（Ars Technica）；Ariana Grande也就歌曲与视频泄露对匿名黑客提起诉讼（The Verge）。融资方面，机器人检测初创公司Spur从Insight Partners获得2亿美元投资（TechCrunch）。此外，MCP初创公司Runlayer起诉Rippling窃取产品创意（TechCrunch），凸显企业创新中的知识产权博弈。这些事件共同表明：科技产品的竞争已从单纯功能创新延伸至合规、安全与法律战场。

汽车 · 20 条

汽车板块今日围绕电动化与自动驾驶展开。沙特王子Alwaleed披露持有Lucid 5%股份，推动股价暴涨25%，为这家现金告急的电动汽车制造商带来重要背书（Electrek）。百度Apollo Go同日启动伦敦Robotaxi路测，并同时与Uber和Freenow（Lyft）合作，标志中国自动驾驶公司首次进入右舵市场（Electrek）。然而特斯拉的FSD再次面临质疑：前测试经理在诉讼中称，由于安全员严重短缺，测试车辆成为“滚动隐患”（Engadget）。大众ID.Polo以低于3万美元起售价上市，已获2.5万订单（Electrek）；宝马iX3订单接近10万，正加速增产（Electrek）。传统车企在廉价电动车领域正形成合围之势，而特斯拉的自动驾驶叙事则面临法律与声誉的双重压力。

item.content:encoded:
News Radar — 科技新闻

2026-07-29 · Window: 24h · Items: 104 · Generated: 2026-07-29 04:30 UTC

Editor's Brief

The tech world is grappling with a potent mix of AI anxiety and strategic realignments. Chip stocks slid across US and Asian markets as jitters over the sustainability of AI spending and a major security scare at OpenAI rattled investors. Simultaneously, a wave of calls from AI experts and employees—including those at OpenAI and Anthropic—is urging a global slowdown in frontier development. In automotive, Lucid got a massive Saudi vote of confidence, while Baidu’s robotaxis began testing in London. On the policy front, the US announced a ban on foreign-made humanoid robots and power inverters, targeting China. The eBay cyberstalking saga concluded with a $56M settlement. Meanwhile, the Hacker News community celebrated a nostalgic Half-Life port to Mac OS 9 and new open-source tools for note-taking and animation.

  • AI market jitters – Chip stocks fell on fears of overvaluation and a security incident at OpenAI (described as "unprecedented" by the company). Over 1,100 AI experts signed an open letter calling for a global slowdown, and staff at OpenAI and Anthropic urged the US to boost oversight. BBC | MIT Technology Review | The Straits Times
  • US bans foreign humanoid robots – The FCC announced a ban on imports of advanced robotic devices and power inverters from foreign adversaries, notably China. The rule covers mobile humanoid and quadruped robots, aiming to boost domestic production. Engadget | The Verge
  • eBay pays $56M to settle cyberstalking case – Three former eBay executives and the company settled with a Massachusetts journalist couple who were harassed with live insects, a bloody pig mask, and other threats in 2019. Ars Technica | The Verge
  • Lucid stock jumps 25% on Saudi prince stake – Saudi billionaire Prince Alwaleed bin Talal disclosed a 5% passive stake in the cash-strapped EV maker, signaling continued Saudi support. Electrek
  • Baidu Apollo Go begins London robotaxi testing – The Chinese company started road testing in London with both Uber and Freenow (Lyft), days after a fully driverless trial in Hong Kong. Electrek
  • Tesla FSD manager sues, claims 'rolling hazards' – A former Houston fleet manager filed a wrongful-termination lawsuit alleging that understaffed robotaxi operations made cars dangerous on public streets. Engadget | Electrek
  • Community highlights: Half-Life on Mac OS 9 – Hacker News lit up with a port of Half-Life to Mac OS 9 (186 points), alongside Show HN projects like Manim in the browser via WebGPU and an open-sourced note-taking app Hubble. Hacker News | Hacker News | Hacker News

Watch next: The AI security scare and the wave of regulatory calls could trigger policy shifts in the coming weeks. The US robot ban may escalate tech decoupling with China. In EVs, watch for Tesla's response to the lawsuit and whether Lucid can capitalize on the Saudi boost. Keep an eye on the Baidu robotaxi expansion into right-hand-drive markets.

AI · 34 items

The AI sector is under intense pressure following a security breach at OpenAI that rattled investor confidence, triggering a sell-off in chip stocks globally. Over 1,100 AI experts have called for a slowdown in frontier development, and staff at OpenAI and Anthropic are urging stronger US oversight. Despite the turmoil, innovation continues: Andrew Ng's startup LearnVector launched a personalized learning platform, and a new agentic IDE called Capuchin was announced. The community is also discussing AI-written fiction on Amazon and policy proposals for GCC.

  • AI stock sell-off – Chip stocks fell as the market reacted to OpenAI's "unprecedented" hack and broader concerns over AI spending. The sell-off was felt in both US and Asian markets. BBC
  • Calls for a global slowdown – More than 1,100 AI experts signed an open letter urging a temporary halt in frontier AI development. Separately, current and former staff at OpenAI and Anthropic pressed US policymakers for stronger oversight. The Straits Times | KuCoin
  • Andrew Ng's LearnVector – The AI educator's new company launched a platform for personalized one-to-one learning experiences, quickly rising to #2 on Hacker News. Hacker News
  • AI-written fiction on Amazon – Data shows a sharp rise in AI-generated book sales from 2023 to 2026, sparking debate on the platform's content policies. Twitter

Signal: The combination of a high-profile security incident and a coordinated expert demand for a pause suggests that the AI industry's regulatory reckoning may be accelerating, with potential implications for investment and deployment timelines.

科技产品 · 40 items

A mix of policy, security, and legal news dominated the tech products landscape. The US announced a ban on foreign-made humanoid robots and power inverters, directly targeting China's robotics exports. eBay's long-running cyberstalking saga ended with a $56M settlement. Meanwhile, bot-detection startup Spur raised $200M from Insight Partners, and Wikimedia Foundation employees expanded their union drive.

  • US bans foreign humanoid robots – The FCC imposed an import ban on advanced mobile robots (humanoid, quadruped) and power inverters from foreign countries, citing national security. The move is widely seen as aimed at Chinese manufacturers. Engadget | The Verge
  • eBay settles cyberstalking case for $56M – eBay and three former executives paid the sum to journalist couple Ina and David Steiner, who were targeted with a bizarre harassment campaign including a bloody pig mask and live insects after critiquing the company. Ars Technica | The Verge
  • Bot-detection startup Spur raises $200M – Spur Intelligence, which identifies human vs bot traffic, secured the funding from Insight Partners, highlighting growing demand for anti-fraud tech. TechCrunch
  • Wikimedia Foundation union drive expands – US-based employees joined UK staff in seeking union recognition, but management has declined to voluntarily recognize it. The Verge

Signal: The US robot ban signals an escalation in tech decoupling, while the eBay settlement and Spur funding underscore the growing legal and security risks in the digital marketplace.

汽车 · 20 items

A dramatic day for EVs: Saudi billionaire Prince Alwaleed took a 5% stake in Lucid, sending shares up 25%. Baidu's Apollo Go began robotaxi road testing in London with both Uber and Lyft's Freenow. A former Tesla manager's lawsuit alleges that the company's Full Self-Driving test fleet was understaffed and dangerous. Volkswagen opened orders for a cheaper ID. Polo EV, and BMW's iX3 orders approached 100,000.

  • Lucid gets Saudi boost – Prince Alwaleed bin Talal disclosed a 5% passive stake in Lucid Group, reassuring investors of continued Saudi backing. The stock jumped 25% on the news. Electrek
  • Baidu Apollo Go launches in London – The robotaxi service started testing on London streets with Uber and Freenow, marking a key expansion after a fully driverless trial in Hong Kong. Electrek
  • Tesla self-driving manager files lawsuit – Former Houston fleet manager Javier Medrano claims the robotaxi operation was so understaffed that vehicles became "rolling hazards on public streets." The lawsuit raises safety concerns ahead of Tesla's planned driverless robotaxi launch. Engadget | Electrek
  • Volkswagen ID. Polo cheaper variant – With a 37 kWh battery and sub-$30,000 price, VW opened orders after already securing 25,000 orders for the standard version. Electrek
  • BMW iX3 orders near 100,000 – BMW is ramping up production of the electric SUV at a record pace to meet strong demand. Electrek

Signal: The convergence of Lucid's financial lifeline, Baidu's global robotaxi push, and Tesla's safety allegations paints a picture of an EV industry at a critical inflection point—capital is flowing, competition is globalizing, but operational risks are being exposed.

The Hacker News community was alive with nostalgia and innovation. The top post by far was a port of Half-Life to Mac OS 9 (186 points), a technical feat that sparked memories and discussions. Other highlights included open-source tools: Hubble, an AI-friendly note-taking app, and a WebGPU-powered version of 3Blue1Brown's Manim animation engine. A thoughtful essay on the difference between buttons and links resonated with designers and developers.

Editor's Brief

Today's entertainment landscape is marked by franchise expansions, political music disputes, and personal milestones in Asia. In Hollywood, the release of the 'Jumanji: Open World' trailer signals the end of a popular trilogy, while Noah Kahan's public condemnation of the White House using his song underscores the ongoing tension between artists and political entities. Meanwhile, the Korean entertainment industry buzzes with actor Moon Geun Young's marriage and new casting announcements, and the Chinese fan community reacts to a resolved incident involving Thai company GMM. Key themes include the push for unionization in VFX, sophomore slumps in streaming, and the growing influence of short-form content in China.

  • Pearl Jam’s Early Years Revealed in New Intimate Photography Book — A new photography book by bassist Jeff Ament offers rare backstage and candid moments from the band's formative decades, appealing to longtime fans and music historians.
  • Evan Rachel Wood Says She’s Not Returning for ‘Practical Magic 2’ Because It’s “Not Following the Book” — The actress expresses disappointment over creative deviations, highlighting the tension between source material and adaptation in legacy sequels.
  • Noah Kahan Calls Out Donald Trump’s Administration For Using “American Cars” Song In White House Social Media Post — A direct rebuke from the artist adds to a growing list of musicians objecting to unsanctioned political use of their work, raising questions about licensing and consent.
  • ‘Jumanji: Open World’ Trailer Sees Core Four Group Of Videogame Avatars Unleashed In Real Life — Sony drops the first full trailer for the franchise's finale, promising a meta twist where the avatars escape into the real world; set for December 2026 release.
  • Moon Geun Young Announces Marriage With Heartfelt Letter — The beloved Korean actress ties the knot with musical actor Jung Pyeong, drawing congratulations and nostalgic reactions from fans.
  • Jennie Hits New Peak Of No. 2 On Billboard Radio Songs Chart With Tame Impala Collab “Dracula” — The BLACKPINK member continues her solo success, climbing to a career-high on US radio and signaling strong cross-over appeal.
  • 泰国娱乐公司GMM再次回应“中国女粉丝被工作人员打”：双方达成和解，此前被暂时停职的工作人员已恢复原有工作职责 — After public outcry, GMM confirms a settlement with the Chinese fan, but the reinstatement of the employee has sparked further debate about accountability in fan-idol interactions.

Watch next for the official 'Jumanji: Open World' marketing rollout ahead of December, any further developments in artist-politics clashes, the trajectory of K-drama viewing figures particularly for Netflix sophomore seasons, and how the GMM incident reshapes Chinese fan community norms.

  • 苹果重夺全球市值第一：苹果收盘市值超越英伟达，后者自2025年6月以来一直占据榜首。这一轮换反映了市场从AI算力硬件向消费电子龙头的偏好转移。来源

  • SpaceX市值已蒸发相当于一个特斯拉，高位回撤超1.2万亿美元。

item.content:encoded:
News Radar — 经济新闻

2026-07-28 · Window: 24h · Items: 121 · Generated: 2026-07-28 04:28 UTC

Editor's Brief

Global markets are caught in a dual shock this morning: a deep semiconductor rout that originated in Seoul and spilled into U.S. and Asian equities, and a sharp decline in oil prices after the U.S. signaled a pause in strikes on Iran. The chip sell-off, led by SK Hynix's 13% plunge, erased billions in market cap and triggered a trading halt on South Korea's Kospi. Meanwhile, China's memory chip maker CXMT staged a stunning 466% debut, becoming the country's largest listed firm by market value, highlighting a stark divergence in AI-related bets. European stocks rose as lower oil prices lifted risk appetite, while the ECB signaled further rate hikes ahead. Investors are rotating into defensive sectors and watching for signals from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh later this week.

  • Chip rout deepens: SK Hynix shares fell 13% in Seoul, dragging the Kospi down 8% and triggering a circuit breaker (CNBC). The sell-off extended to U.S. markets, with Nvidia losing its crown as the world's most valuable company to Apple (CNBC).
  • Oil drops 9% on U.S.-Iran de-escalation: Brent crude fell below $88/barrel after President Trump indicated a pause in hostilities, easing fears of a supply disruption in the Strait of Hormuz (The Guardian).
  • CXMT's record IPO: ChangXin Memory Technologies surged 466% on its Shanghai debut, valuing it at 3.3 trillion yuan, surpassing ICBC. Nomura sees potential for the stock to double again as the firm targets 18% global DRAM market share by 2028 (SCMP).
  • U.S.-Korea tech correlation worry: The 60-day correlation between the Kospi and Nasdaq 100 hit 0.50, the highest since 2021, raising concerns about contagion risk for global portfolios (CNBC).
  • European stocks rally on oil relief: The STOXX 600 closed higher as falling crude boosted consumer discretionary and transport sectors (Investing.com).
  • ECB hawkish: ECB Governing Council member Kazimir said a September rate hike is likely needed even if the outlook improves (Reuters).
  • LVMH signals luxury recovery: Fashion and leather division reported 1% organic growth in Q2, ending seven quarters of decline, a positive sign for the sector's exposure to Chinese demand (SCMP).

Watch next: All eyes are on Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference this week. Prediction markets suggest he will address last week's oil supply shock (CNBC). Separately, the Hong Kong IPO of CATL-backed NASN Intelligent Tech could test investor appetite for smart-driving plays. The divergence between Western AI hardware stocks and Chinese memory chip stocks will be a key narrative this week.

美股 · 64 items

U.S. equity markets are under pressure from a deepening semiconductor sell-off that began in Asia. Apple reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company as Nvidia lost over $1 trillion in market cap since June. Oil's sharp decline is providing some relief, but the Fed's messaging later this week will be critical for rate-sensitive sectors.

  • SK Hynix shares plunge 13% in Seoul as chip sell-off deepens — The rout in South Korean chipmakers has direct implications for U.S. semiconductor ETFs and holders of Samsung and SK Hynix ADRs.
  • Apple ends day as world's most valuable company, passing Nvidia — Nvidia's 60% peak-to-trough decline signals waning AI euphoria; Apple's relative stability highlights rotation to quality.
  • Oil prices drop more than 2% as a pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities raises de-escalation hopes — A sustained decline in crude could dampen inflationary pressure and support consumer discretionary stocks.
  • Trump backs 'fantastic' Warsh while calling for lower rates — Political pressure on the Fed to cut rates conflicts with the need to manage supply-side inflation from oil.

Signal: The Kospi-Nasdaq correlation at 0.50 suggests any further weakness in Korean memory stocks will directly weigh on U.S. tech indexes.
